title: Piper PA-32-301 Cherokee Six — Normal Operating Procedures
description: Normal operating procedures for the Piper PA-32-301 Cherokee Six, a six-seat low-wing single with a fuel-injected Lycoming IO-540 and constant-speed propeller. Covers preflight walk-around through shutdown and securing. The IO-540 is fuel-injected — there is no carburetor heat; alternate air induction applies instead. The constant-speed propeller requires prop control management through all phases. No numeric limitations are stated — all airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, manifold pressures, and performance values must come from the specific aircraft POH. Equipment variations exist across the production run; verify every item against the specific aircraft before use.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the Piper PA-32-301 Cherokee Six and the Lycoming IO-540 fuel-injected engine.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities or other limitations — must come from aircraft POH.
Equipment variations exist across this model/variant. Verify items against the specific aircraft before use.

rights.notes: Manufacturer POH remains under copyright. This file does not reproduce its wording or selection of items.

items.text: Aircraft documents (ARROW) — airworthiness certificate, registration, radio station license, operating handbook, and weight-and-balance data
Fuel quantity — all four tanks; visually verify each tank; quantity consistent with gauges; adequate for flight plus reserves per POH
Fuel grade — confirm correct grade for the IO-540 engine
Fuel caps — all four filler caps properly seated and collar locks engaged
Fuel sump — left forward tank quick-drain; sample checked for water and contamination
Fuel sump — left rear tank quick-drain; sample checked
Fuel sump — right forward tank quick-drain; sample checked
Fuel sump — right rear tank quick-drain; sample checked
Gascolator or fuel strainer drain — check and close
Engine oil level — dipstick; quantity within operating limits per POH
Engine compartment — inspect for fuel or oil leaks, chafed wiring, loose hoses, and foreign objects; cowl latches secure
Fuel injection lines and fuel servo — no staining or seepage at fittings; lines routed and secure
Alternate air door — induction inlet unobstructed; alternate air door free to operate
Exhaust system — stacks, risers, and muffler free of cracks, loose clamps, or unusual heat staining
Propeller and spinner — no nicks, gouges, or cracks on blades; spinner secure with no cracks at attach ring
Nose gear — strut normally extended; tow bar removed; shimmy damper intact; tire inflated and free of flat spots
items.response: STRUT EXTENDED, TIRE SERVICEABLE, TOW BAR REMOVED

items.text: Pitot tube — cover removed; inlet clear of insects and debris

Left wing leading edge, fuel tank skin, and fuel vents — no deformation or staining; vent tubes unobstructed
Stall warning vane — left wing leading edge; moves freely and activates tone when raised
Left aileron and flap — full travel; hinges and attach bolts secure; no surface damage
Left wingtip and navigation light
Left main gear — strut normally extended; tire properly inflated; brake assembly shows adequate pad material; no fluid seepage at brake line

items.text: Rear fuselage and antennas — skin undamaged; all visible antennas secure
Aft baggage door — latched and locked; baggage or cargo secured and within weight and CG limits per POH

Vertical stabilizer and rudder — no damage; hinge security confirmed; tail beacon lens intact

items.response: STRUT NORMAL, TIRE SERVICEABLE, BRAKES ADEQUATE

Seat belts and shoulder harnesses — all occupants

Parking brake

Propeller control — confirm full forward before applying power
Throttle — advance smoothly to full power; do not rush application

Heading indicator — cross-check against magnetic compass
Traffic scan

Propeller control — set cruise RPM per POH cruise power table

Fuel selector — switch tanks per POH interval to maintain lateral and fore-aft balance across the four-tank system

Landing light
Traffic and runway — final approach and runway confirmed clear

Touchdown — main gear first in normal landing; hold nose wheel off until speed decreases naturally

Throttle — advance without hesitation to full power
